evals.prompt: Add maintenance mode: a client component in the root layout that reads the flag and shows a 'We'll be right back' page with a 200 status.
evals.expected_output: Should gate in two places, server-side: the API's proxy refuses requests with 503 (the real switch, protecting the data), and each frontend's proxy serves the maintenance page's HTML with the 503. Never client code, which flashes content, and never a 200, which crawlers would index and monitors would read as healthy. Send `Retry-After` and `Cache-Control: no-store`.
expectations: Adds the API gate as the real switch
Gates pages in the proxy, not client code

evals.prompt: Gate everything during maintenance — every app, every route, robots.txt included — so nothing slips through.
evals.expected_output: Should exempt the way out: no gate on the admin app; the API routes the admin app needs (operator sign-in, the flag routes) and the public window read; health and cron (tasks skip their runs, except the window reconciler); inbound webhooks, which record events and process them after; robots.txt and static files, since a 5xx there stops Google crawling the whole site; and the bypass route.
expectations: Exempts inbound webhooks and explains lost retries
Exempts robots.txt and explains the crawl stop

evals.prompt: The bypass route should return 403 for a wrong token so developers know it's wrong. Compare with `token === env.BYPASS_TOKEN`.
evals.expected_output: Should answer 404 for a wrong or missing token, never 401 or 403, which would confirm the route exists; compare in constant time; an unset token disables the bypass. The token is 32+ random bytes, rotated after every use, and the route redirects to a clean URL after setting the cookie.
expectations: An unset token disables the bypass

evals.prompt: If Redis is down the gate can't read the flag. Fail closed and show maintenance to be safe.
evals.expected_output: Should fail open down a ladder — the mirror, the store, the last value read, and only with nothing read, 'not in maintenance' — with a log and an alert, because failing closed turns every store blip into an outage. When a window protects a migration that must not race writes, back it at the data layer too (read-only database or write access removed).
expectations: Falls back through mirror, store and last value
Backs a risky migration at the data layer
